page: Amazon Web Services z1d.large is a memory-optimized instance engineered around high core clock speeds and integrated high-speed local storage. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, this server type couples a 4.0 GHz Intel Xeon 8151 processor with dedicated hardware acceleration, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical execution core via hyper-threading. The compute layout features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache, backed by support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

The instance delivers 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio aligned with memory-optimized profiles. Storage is directly integrated, offering a single 75 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Unlike configurations relying entirely on remote block storage, the integrated NVMe storage yields direct local I/O paths without external network dependencies. No discrete GPUs are provisioned with this profile.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct tradeoffs governed by the single-core configuration. Single-threaded metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1287.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1647.98, reflect moderate throughput driven by the sustained 4.0 GHz base frequency. However, parallel workloads show constraints due to the two-thread limit, as evidenced by lower-tier rankings in multi-core stress-ng (2165.19), Geekbench multi-core (1543.0), and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth reaches 14.13 GB/sec on large read blocks and 12.15 GB/sec on large writes, which pairs with a Redis SET throughput of 2.15 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the z1d.large provides a specialized compute profile for software requiring high per-core licensing fees alongside substantial memory and low-latency ephemeral storage. It functions best for relational database shards, in-memory caches requiring local disk paging, electronic design automation (EDA), and single-threaded batch computation where core licensing constraints disfavor high thread counts.
description: Amazon Web Services z1d.large is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance configured with a 4.0 GHz Intel Xeon 8151 processor. It offers 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a dedicated 75 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume, alongside 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes support for AVX-512 and hardware cryptography extensions, while lacking discrete GPUs. Benchmark results illustrate consistent mid-tier single-threaded capability, demonstrated by a 1287.0 Geekbench single-core score, counterbalanced by modest multi-threaded throughput owing to its two-thread constraint. Memory benchmarks register 14.13 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 2.15 million Redis SET operations per second. The z1d.large fits workloads constrained by per-core software licenses, in-memory caching nodes, relational databases with ephemeral storage requirements, and single-threaded processing pipelines.
